27 A teacher is explaining diffraction to a group of students.
Which piece of apparatus is most appropriate for the teacher to use to demonstrate diffraction?
A
a long spring
B
a ripple tank
C
a rope
D
a stretched string

hints: Recall what diffraction looks like: plane wavefronts passing a gap of width similar to the wavelength and then spreading into circular wavefronts.
Think about which apparatus lets you see a two-dimensional wavefront from above and lets you place barriers with gaps in the path of the wave.
Compare a ripple tank with a long spring, rope and stretched string, which all confine the wave to travel only along one line.
walkthrough: Identify the effect to show: diffraction is the spreading of waves when they pass through a gap or pass an edge, most clearly seen when gap width is similar to wavelength.
Recall the requirement for a clear demonstration: you need to see the shape of wavefronts before and after the obstacle in two dimensions.
Consider a ripple tank: a dipper creates straight water wavefronts that can be viewed from above, and metal barriers can form single slits and edges.
Observe what happens: after the gap the straight fronts become curved and spread into the shadow region, showing diffraction directly.

Contrast with a long spring, rope and stretched string: they guide waves along one line and are used for longitudinal waves, transverse pulses and stationary waves, not for spreading through apertures.
Therefore the ripple tank is the most appropriate apparatus for this demonstration. This is option B

A.explanation: A long spring is good for showing longitudinal pulses and reflection, but it is one-dimensional and cannot show spreading through a gap or around an obstacle.

B.explanation: A ripple tank shows water wavefronts spreading after passing a narrow gap or barrier, which is direct visual evidence of diffraction.

C.explanation: A rope is good for showing transverse pulses and stationary waves, but it is one-dimensional and cannot show diffraction through an aperture.

D.explanation: A stretched string is good for showing stationary waves and harmonics, but it does not allow a wave to spread in two dimensions past an obstacle.
